Park Forest schedules memorial for former trustee Viola Baecher
Former Park Forest Trustee Viola Baecher will be honored at a memorial gathering on October 9 following decades of service as an educator and public servant. The village recognizes her historic role as its first African American woman trustee along with her contributions beyond local government.
A memorial gathering for former Park Forest Trustee Viola Baecher is scheduled for Friday, October 9, at 12:30 p.m. at the Unitarian Universalist Community Church on Sycamore Drive in Park Forest, according to an Oct. 8 announcement.
Baecher was elected Village trustee in 1988 and became the first African American woman to serve on the Park Forest Board of Trustees. She dedicated much of her life to public service, education, and promoting cultural heritage. Her work extended into classrooms, community organizations, and historical research.
Born August 19, 1943, in Zanesville, Ohio, to Granville William Reed Jr. and Anita Ozelle Reed, Baecher considered Chicago her hometown. After graduating from Marshall High School, she earned a bachelor's degree from Roosevelt University and a master's degree from the University of Chicago's School of Social Service Administration. At Rich Central High School, she worked as a social worker and head cheerleading coach, where she supported students and families, led crisis response teams, directed Martin Luther King Jr. assemblies, and sponsored student organizations such as the chess club and Afro Club.
Baecher’s commitment continued in local government when she represented residents as a member of the Park Forest Village Board after her historic election in 1988. She narrowly lost reelection in 1990 but sought the Village presidency in 1991, where she finished second to Pat Kelly.
Genealogy was another defining passion for Baecher; she devoted years to documenting African American family histories, tracing her ancestry back generations across several states. Her findings were shared through presentations with groups like the Park Forest Historical Society, encouraging others to research their own family stories: “It's especially important for African Americans,” Baecher told The Beverly Review. “We just don't have enough of these incredibly positive stories for people to see and to appreciate their own stories.”
Park Forest honors Viola Baecher’s service with memorial bunting at Village Hall’s south façade while expressing condolences to all who feel her loss. Memorial contributions may be made to charitable organizations including Greater Chicago Food Depository or Mary's Center in Washington D.C., among others.
The Village operates under a council-manager government featuring a mayor and six trustees as its governing body; it promotes community health through commissions and programs while supporting sustainability efforts recognized by accolades for town planning practices, according to the official website.
